subtopic: Purpose and Planning of a Field Visit
stem: Choose the correct alternative and complete the sentence: Visiting a given place and gaining first hand information is known as ______.
solution: **(A)** Field visit. Visiting a place and gaining first hand information about it by direct observation is a field visit. During it we observe the relief, water bodies, vegetation, soil, agriculture and settlements of the region and record them in our notebooks. A census counts the population, and health tourism is travel for medical treatment, so neither of them is a visit made to observe a place.

stem: Choose the correct alternative and complete the sentence: India is famous for ______ all over the world.
solution: **(D)** Spices. India is famous all over the world for its spices, and spices are among the main exports of India along with tea, mangoes, coffee, leather goods, iron ore and cotton and silk textiles. Coffee is the product Brazil is known for: Brazil is called the 'coffee pot' of the world, and coffee and cocoa are among Brazil's exports.

stem: Choose the correct alternative and complete the sentence: Brazil is the most populated country in the ______ continent.
solution: **(C)** South America. Brazil lies in the northern part of the South American continent and is the largest country of that continent in both area and population. Asia is the continent of India, which is the second most populous country in the world.

stem: Choose the correct alternative and complete the sentence: The Indian Standard Time is ahead by ______ from the Greenwich Meridian Time.
solution: **(B)** 5 Hours 30 Minutes. India has only one standard time zone. Its standard meridian is the \(82.5^\circ\) E longitude, which passes through Allahabad (Prayagraj). Local time changes by 4 minutes for every degree of longitude, so the time difference from Greenwich (\(0^\circ\)) is \(82.5 \times 4 = 330\) minutes. \(\therefore\) IST is 330 minutes, that is 5 hours 30 minutes, ahead of Greenwich Mean Time.

stem: Identify the wrong pair:

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon river basin \(\rightarrow\) North of Brazil

options.label: B
options.text: Puraguaco river basin \(\rightarrow\) West of Brazil

options.label: C
options.text: Sao Francisco river basin \(\rightarrow\) East of Brazil

options.label: D
options.text: Paraguay and Parana river basin \(\rightarrow\) South-West of Brazil

solution: **(B)** Puraguaco river basin \(\rightarrow\) West of Brazil. The Puraguaco is a short coastal river that collects its headwaters along the Great Escarpment and enters the Atlantic Ocean near the town of Salvador, so its basin lies in the EAST of Brazil, not the west. The other pairs are correct: the Amazon basin occupies the north, the Sao Francisco basin occupies the eastern portion of the highlands, and the Paraguay-Parana system lies in the south-west of Brazil.

stem: Identify the wrong pair:

options.label: C
options.text: Centre of India \(\rightarrow\) Tropic of Capricorn

solution: **(C)** Centre of India \(\rightarrow\) Tropic of Capricorn. The line passing through the middle of India is the Tropic of Cancer, which is why India is considered a tropical country. The Tropic of Capricorn lies in the southern hemisphere and passes through the southern part of Brazil. The other pairs are correct: India's climate is of the monsoon type, the Equator passes through the northern part of Brazil, and the Atlantic Ocean lies to the east of Brazil.

stem: Write a short note (any two of Q. 3): India - location and extent.
solution: India - location and extent: India lies in the northern and eastern hemispheres of the Earth, in the southern part of the Asian continent. The mainland of India extends from \(8^\circ 4'\) N to \(37^\circ 6'\) N latitudes and from \(68^\circ 7'\) E to \(97^\circ 25'\) E longitudes. Indira Point, the southernmost tip of India, lies on the \(6^\circ 45'\) N parallel. The Tropic of Cancer passes through the middle of the country, so India is considered a tropical country. India is bordered by Pakistan and Afghanistan in the north-west, China, Nepal and Bhutan in the north, Myanmar and Bangladesh in the east, and Sri Lanka lies to the south across the sea. It has the Arabian Sea to the west, the Bay of Bengal to the east and the Indian Ocean to the south. The southern part of India, tapering into the Indian Ocean, is called the Peninsula. The time difference between the two extreme points of India is 2 hours, but India keeps one standard time based on the \(82.5^\circ\) E meridian.

stem: Write a short note (any two of Q. 3): Escarpment.
solution: Escarpment: An escarpment is a long, very steep slope or cliff that marks the edge of a plateau or highland. In Brazil the Great Escarpment forms the eastern edge of the Brazilian Highlands. Though it occupies a very small area, the nature of its slope and its effect on the climate make it a separate physiographic division of Brazil. Its altitude here is about 790 m; in some regions the height decreases gradually, and the escarpment is very steep particularly from Sao Paulo to Porto Alegre. It acts as a barrier to the South-East Trade winds, so the coastal side receives orographic rainfall, while the north-eastern part of the highlands lies in the rain shadow; the dry region to the north of this area is called the 'Drought Quadrilateral'. Many short coastal rivers that enter the Atlantic Ocean, such as the Puraguaco, collect their headwaters along the escarpment.

stem: Write a short note (any two of Q. 3): Importance of Indian Ocean.
solution: Importance of Indian Ocean: (1) The Indian Ocean, together with the Himalayas, exerts a great influence on the climate of India and on the origin of the monsoons. In summer a low pressure area develops over the Punjab plains and the Thar desert, and moisture-laden winds blow from the high pressure region over the Indian Ocean towards the mainland; these South-West monsoon winds bring most of India's rainfall. (2) In the retreating season the winds blow back from the north-east towards the Indian Ocean and give rainfall again to parts of the Peninsula. (3) The Peninsula of India tapers into the Indian Ocean, so India has a long coastline of about 7500 km with ports on both its coasts. (4) India stands at the head of the Indian Ocean on the sea routes between the east and the west, which helps its foreign trade. (5) The ocean is a source of fish and other marine resources for the coastal people.

stem: Give geographical reason (any two of Q. 5): India is a major trading partner for other countries of the world.
solution: (1) India produces and exports a wide range of goods, such as tea, mangoes, coffee, spices, leather and leather goods, iron ore and cotton and silk textiles, which are in demand all over the world. (2) With a very large population and a growing economy, India is considered a global market, so it also imports large quantities of petroleum, machines, precious stones, gold and silver, paper and medicines. (3) Economic reforms from time to time have speeded up India's economic development and opened its economy to foreign trade and investment. (4) India's location at the head of the Indian Ocean, with a long coastline and many ports, places it on the sea routes between the east and the west. Therefore India trades with many countries such as the UK, the USA, Germany, Japan, China and Russia, and is a major trading partner for other countries of the world.

stem: Give geographical reason (any two of Q. 5): Brazil does not receive snowfall.
solution: (1) Brazil is a tropical country: most of it lies in the tropical zone and the Equator passes through its northern part, so temperatures are high throughout the year. (2) Brazil has no very high mountains; most of its highlands are only 500 to 1000 m high, so altitude does not lower the temperature to freezing. (3) The country is surrounded by the Atlantic Ocean on the east, so the coast experiences a mild and humid climate. Only in exceptional conditions do cold polar air masses from the south reach southern Brazil and cause snowfall there, as recorded in 1879, 1957 and 1985. Hence Brazil normally does not receive snowfall.

stem: Give geographical reason (any two of Q. 5): Settlements are sparse in North-Eastern Brazil.
solution: (1) The Great Escarpment acts as a barrier to the South-East Trade winds, so the north-eastern part of the Brazilian Highlands lies in a rain shadow and receives very little rainfall. (2) This region, called the 'Drought Quadrilateral', suffers from extreme droughts, which make it difficult to practise agriculture. (3) Shortage of water and poor agriculture mean that few people can earn a living here; the north-east is traditionally the poorest part of Brazil and has few large industries. Hence the settlements in north-eastern Brazil are sparse.

stem: Give geographical reason (any two of Q. 5): Telecom industry has become one of the fastest growing sector in India.
solution: (1) With the explosion of electronic media, the demand for communication services has grown very fast in India. (2) In this era of information and communication, digitally enhanced devices such as mobile phones, the Internet and satellites are widening the reach of communication technology. (3) India's large population provides a huge market of users for mobile phones and the Internet, in cities as well as in villages. (4) Business, trade, banking, education and administration increasingly depend on quick communication. Therefore the telecom industry has become one of the fastest growing sectors in India.

subtopic: Purpose and Planning of a Field Visit
stem: Answer in detail (any two of Q. 7): What is field visit? What precautions you will take when you visit a sea coast?
solution:
Field visit: Visiting a given place and gaining first hand information about it by direct observation is called a field visit. During a field visit we observe and note down the relief, water bodies, vegetation, soil, agriculture, human settlements and settlement patterns of the region, collect information through questionnaires and interviews, click photographs and later write a report. It helps us to apply our geographical knowledge to a real region.

Precautions while visiting a sea coast:
- Find out the timings of high tide and low tide before going to the beach or to a sea fort, and return from the shore before the tide comes in.
- Follow the instructions of the teachers and stay together in the group; do not wander away alone.
- Do not enter deep water or swim in the sea, and keep away from slippery rocks, steep cliffs and strong waves.
- Carry drinking water, a cap and first-aid material, and protect yourself from the sun.
- Do not throw plastic or other litter on the beach or into the sea; collect it and dispose of it properly.
- Do not disturb or harm marine plants and animals, and respect the local people and their occupations such as fishing.

stem: Answer in detail (any two of Q. 7): Write detailed information on Himalayan Mountains.
solution: Himalayan Mountains: (1) The Himalayas are one of the young fold mountains of the world and a major mountain system of the Asian continent. They extend from the Pamir Knot in Tajikistan towards the east, and in India they stretch from Jammu and Kashmir to Arunachal Pradesh. (2) The Himalayas are not a single range but many parallel ranges. From south to north they are the Siwaliks, the Lesser Himalayas, the Greater Himalayas (Himadri) and the Trans Himalayan ranges. The Siwaliks, the southernmost, are also the youngest; the ranges become older towards the north. (3) From west to east they are divided into the Western (Kashmir) Himalayas, the Central (Kumaun) Himalayas and the Eastern (Assam) Himalayas. (4) Most of the major rivers of the north, such as the Ganga, the Indus and their tributaries, rise from Himalayan glaciers; they are perennial and their discharge increases in summer when the glaciers melt. (5) The Himalayas strongly influence India's climate: they obstruct the very cold winds blowing from the north, and they stop the moisture-laden South-West monsoon winds, causing orographic rainfall over northern India. In winter the temperature in the high mountains drops to -40 degrees Celsius. (6) Forests vary with altitude: mixed forests with sal at the foothills, coniferous trees such as pine, deodar and fir at medium altitude and seasonally flowering plants higher up; snow leopards and yaks live in the snow-capped regions.

stem: Answer in detail (any two of Q. 7): What are the major causes of degradation of forest in Brazil and India?
solution:
Brazil:
- Deforestation: large areas of the Amazon rainforest are being cleared for timber and to make land available for farming, settlements and roads. A survey done in 2016 found that about 5831 sq. km of forest land in Brazil had already degraded in that year.
- Slash and burn agriculture (Roca): in this shifting agriculture a patch of forest is cleared by cutting and burning, cultivated for a few years and then abandoned.
- Illegal smuggling of wild animals, which disturbs the forest ecosystem.
- Pollution.

India:
- Rapid deforestation to meet the needs of a large and growing population for agricultural land, settlements, fuelwood and timber.
- Shifting cultivation similar to Roca in some hilly and forested areas.
- Poaching of wild animals.
- Pollution.

Because of these causes forest cover is shrinking in both countries and many endemic species of plants and animals are on the verge of extinction. Therefore forests need conservation in Brazil as well as in India.
